title: SMS filter extension
summary: Live rule evaluation on incoming messages — iPhone's strong surface
description:
CURRENT STATE: nothing built. API verified by reading iOS SDK 26.2 headers.

Implement ILMessageFilterExtension with ILMessageFilterQueryHandling. handleQueryRequest:context:completion: runs LIVE when a message arrives and carries sender, messageBody and receiverISOCountryCode — so all seven rule types work here by calling F002's evaluate directly. No expansion, no limit.

THIS IS WHY SMS IS IN RELEASE 1. It is the only iPhone surface where rules run live; iPhone calls are expansion-limited. Shipping calls alone would have given iPhone only its weak half.

VERDICT IS LIMITED, LOGIC IS NOT: ILMessageFilterAction tops out at Junk (also Promotion and Transaction, with iOS 16+ sub-actions). It cannot delete a message or stop delivery — the message still arrives, it just lands in the Junk folder. The UI must say this plainly rather than promising blocking.

UNKNOWN SENDERS ONLY: the extension is not consulted for senders in Contacts or with prior conversation history. A rule cannot filter someone the user has previously messaged. This surprises people and must be stated.

OFFLINE BY DEFAULT: the query handler has no network. deferQueryRequestToNetworkWithCompletion: exists for an HTTPS call to a service declared in Info.plist, but release 1 has no server and does not need one — everything is answered on-device by F002.

MEMORY: same extension constraints as the Call Directory. Answer one question without loading the whole dataset.

CAPABILITIES QUERY: ILMessageFilterCapabilitiesQueryHandling (iOS 16+) declares which sub-actions we support. Decide whether to use sub-categories or only Junk.

SHARING: rules and datasets via the App Group, same as the Call Directory extension.
